protocol.name: denial_pet_v1

description.summary: desktop pets that the user can give to a window

protocol.description:
A pet is a layer surface the user can drag onto a window's edge or corner. The window then carries it: the pet moves, hides and shows with the window until the window lets go of it.
The compositor and its shell do all the geometry. A pet says which point of it holds on, what may hold it and how it is stacked; it never learns where any window is, how big, which one or whose. It is given a window only where the user drops it, after a drag the compositor runs from a press on the pet, so it cannot probe for windows by itself. While held, its layer surface's anchors and margins are ignored, so it cannot move itself.
Version 2 lets a pet watch the pointer: it learns which way the pointer is from it, never how far.
Version 3 tells a pet how fast the user drags it, so it can sway as it is carried about. With it, the pet can work out roughly where it was dropped, and so roughly where the window that holds it is.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the wl_surface is not a layer surface

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has a pet object

request.name: get_pet

description.summary: make a layer surface a pet

request.description: The surface must have the zwlr_layer_surface_v1 role. Until the pet is held, the layer surface is placed by its own anchors and margins as before.

description.summary: a layer surface the user can give to a window

enum.name: hold
enum.description: Edges and corners of a window's frame as the user sees it, including any decorations the compositor draws. Each is a single bit, so that set_holds can take several.

entry.name: above
entry.summary: just above its window, below the window's popups

entry.name: below
entry.summary: just below its window, which hides what of the pet it covers

request.name: destroy

description.summary: the surface is a plain layer surface again

request.description: A held pet is let go and goes back to its anchors and margins.

request.name: set_anchor

description.summary: the point of the pet that holds on

request.description: In surface-local logical coordinates. A window holds the pet by this point, so it stays put when the surface resizes; it is also the point that snaps to a window while the user drags the pet. It takes effect at once. The default is the middle of the surface's bottom edge.

request.name: set_holds
request.description: A bitfield of hold values, or-ed together. The default is none: the pet is never held. It applies to the next drag. Unknown bits are ignored.

description.summary: how the pet is stacked while held

request.name: move
request.description: Send this from a pointer button press on the pet, with the press's serial. The compositor then moves the pet with the pointer, and the pet gets no pointer events until the button is released. A serial that is not a current press on the pet is ignored. The drag ends in a placed or a held event.

request.name: watch_pointer

description.summary: the pet wants to know where the pointer is

request.description: From now on the pet is sent pointer events: which way the pointer is from its anchor, about once a second, when that changes.

request.name: ignore_pointer

description.summary: the pet stops watching the pointer

request.description: No more pointer events are sent. Watching is off by default.

event.name: placed

description.summary: the user let the pet go free

event.description: Where the pet's top left now is, in logical pixels from its output's top left; it may be outside that output, on another one. The pet stays there until it sets new layer surface anchors or margins, and should set ones that keep it there.

event.name: held

description.summary: the user let the pet go on a window

event.description: Which kind of hold has it: one of the values it accepts. Nothing more is told about the window.

event.name: carried

description.summary: its window, or the user, is moving it

event.description:
The velocity at which the held pet moves on screen because its window moves, resizes or is animated, in logical pixels per second, x to the right and y down. Sent while it changes, at most once a frame or so; zero when it stops.
Before version 3, nothing is sent while the user drags the pet. From version 3, it is also sent while the user drags it, as the pointer moves it, and zero before it is placed or held. With it the pet can work out roughly where it was dropped.

event.name: released

description.summary: its window let go of the pet

event.description: The window closed, maximized or went fullscreen. The pet is back at its anchors and margins.

event.name: pointer
event.description: The direction from the pet's anchor to the pointer, as the user sees them: a unit vector, x to the right and y down. Never how far it is, so the pet cannot tell where the pointer is. Sent while the pet watches the pointer, at most about once a second, when the direction has changed. Nothing is sent while the user drags the pet, or while the pointer is on its anchor.
